newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl threatened to resign over budget woes - paper.
newsitem.headline: Kohl threatened to resign over budget woes - paper.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl threatened to resign on several occasions last week when his coalition was unable to agree on measures to fill budget holes, the Hamburger Morgenpost newspaper reported on Monday.

The newspaper quoted coalition sources saying that Kohl had offered to quit a total of four times during two crisis meetings held in his chancellery last Sunday and Tuesday. Kohl has reportedly offered to resign on several occasions in the last year.
A government spokesman had no immediate comment on the report.

"Chancellor Helmut Kohl threatened repeatedly to resign in the dispute over the 1998 budget," the newspaper said, quoting sources from Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) and the centrist Free Democrats (FDP).

Last November Kohl threatened to resign amid a row over the 1997 budget, according to coalition sources. But commentators said they believed that was an empty threat that Kohl was easily talked out of because leaders of both Kohl's CDU and FDP realise there are few palatable alternatives to remaining in the coalition.
The threat to quit in November was believed to be the first time since a similar row over taxes in 1988 that Kohl had used such a warning. Such threats have been rare during Kohl's 14-year-long rule.
